name: Augustine of Canterbury
knownFor: Monk of Gregory the Great's monastery sent by Gregory to the English, who baptized King Ethelbert's people of Kent and became the first archbishop of Canterbury.
dates: Sent by Gregory in 596 and landed in Britain in 597, by Bede's own years. His epitaph gives his death on 26 May, with no year; Bede tells it after the ordinations he dates to 604
place: Rome; Kent, with his see at Canterbury
tradition: The Roman Church in the Age of Gregory the Great
role: Monk and provost; missionary; first archbishop of Canterbury

keyWorks.title: Questions to Gregory the Great, with Gregory's answers
keyWorks.about: nine questions on a bishop's life and income, the differing customs of the churches, theft from the church, marriage, ordaining bishops, the bishops of Gaul and Britain, and purity at baptism and communion; kept as Bede copied them, and in the Latin of Gregory's Register

traces: Bede says King Ethelbert believed and was baptized, and gave the monks a home at Canterbury; Gregory wrote that over ten thousand English were reported baptized one Christmas.
Gregory sent him the pallium and a plan for twelve bishops, and put all the bishops of Britain in his care. In 604, Bede says, he ordained Mellitus and Justus as bishops.
remembered: His epitaph, which Bede copies, calls him the first archbishop of Canterbury, sent by Gregory and supported with miracles, who brought King Ethelbert and his nation from idols to the faith of Christ.
Bede calls him the beloved of God, Father Augustine. Gregory's letter to him on his miracles tells him to rejoice with fear.

uncertain: Bede, the main witness, wrote his History long after the mission and is hostile to the Britons, whom he calls "that perfidious nation". He tells the second meeting with the British bishops, after the first at Augustine's Oak, with the hedge "is said" on Augustine's warning, and presents the later slaughter of the Bangor monks as its fulfilment.

Who ordained him at Arles. Bede names Aetherius, archbishop of that city; L. Cecil Jane's note to Bede says Aetherius was really archbishop of Lyons. Nicola Turchi's note to Gregory's letters names Vergilius of Arles. Gregory says only that he was made bishop by the bishops of the Germanies. Gregory's letter to Eulogius has him made bishop before he was brought to the English; Bede has him go to Arles after the king's baptism.

The questions and answers. Paul Ewald and Ludwig Hartmann, editing Gregory's Register in the Monumenta Germaniae Historica, say they have often been doubted, and judge them genuine; they report Theodor Mommsen's view that only extracts survive. James Barmby, translating the Register, holds Bede's copy the most authentic. Boniface, in a letter the editors date to 735, reported that no copy could be found at Rome.

The year of his death. Bede tells it after the ordinations he dates to 604 and gives no year of his own; the epitaph gives 26 May, in King Ethelbert's reign. Paul Ewald and Ludwig Hartmann have Laurentius succeed him in 606.
The date of Ethelbert's baptism. Bede gives none. Turchi dates it to Christmas 597, from Gregory's letter to Eulogius, which reports the ten thousand baptized at Christmas without naming the king.

His monastery. Gregory calls him the former provost of his monastery and does not name it. L. Cecil Jane's note to Bede names the monastery of Saint Anthony at Rome and calls him a Benedictine; no letter of Gregory used here says either.
